summary: Craig Jamieson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Cambridge, attested in 2002 and in 2012 as curator for the South Asia manuscript collection, and was a fellow at Queens' College, Cambridge, attested in 2012.
Craig Preston is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia under Joe Bransford Wilson and with Jeffrey Hopkins from 1980 to 1981.

Cristina Pecchia is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Sapienza University of Rome (~1999–2003) under Raniero Gnoli, Raffaele Torella, and Corrado Pensa, also studying at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner (2000). Around 2009, she was a project researcher at IKGA.

Csaba Dezső is an Indologist who completed master's degrees at Eötvös Loránd University (~1991–1997) and a PhD at the University of Oxford (1998–2004) under Alexis Sanderson. Around 2003, he served as an Assistant Lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University.

Csaba Kiss is an Indologist who earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (2003–2009) under Alexis Sanderson. He has held posts as a research assistant at Eötvös Loránd University and at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2024).

Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She held posts as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Toronto (attested 2017) and at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2018).

Culadasa (1944–2021) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under traditional teacher Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu and taught Matthew Immergut. Attested in 2011, he served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha.
Cuma Ozkan is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter, attested in 2013.

Cuong T. Mai works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaii and a PhD at Indiana University under John R. McRae (attested 2009), later serving as an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Keizaburō Mizuno and doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, and held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2009).
Cynthia Col is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. She studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) under Mark C. Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.

Cyril Henry Philips (1912–2005) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Liverpool (~1931–1934) and SOAS (~1934–1938). He served as Director of SOAS (~1956–1976) and held a post at the University of London (1972–1976).

Cyrus Stearns is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA under Turrell V. Wylie and a PhD (-1996) under Leonard van der Kuijp at the University of Washington, studied under multiple traditional teachers, and worked as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.

Cécile Ducher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Matthew T. Kapstein (-2017) and later worked there as a research fellow.

D. C. Lau (1921–2010) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. After studying at the University of Hong Kong (~1939–1946), he taught Heather Stoddard and held posts at SOAS (~1950–1978) and University College London (1970–1978).
D. C. Sarasvati is an Indologist who studied under V. Raghavan (attested 1978). She served as a Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras from 1964 to 1965.

D. Dennis Hudson (1938–2006) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who taught Andrew P. Tuck. He served as a Professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College from circa 1970 to 2004.

D. Neil Schmid is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, Waseda University, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a doctoral student under Victor H. Mair.

Dagfinn Føllesdal is a philosopher who studied at the University of Oslo (~1950–1957) and Harvard (~1957–1961) under Willard Van Orman Quine, and taught Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at the University of Oslo (~1967–1999) and Stanford University (~1968–2010).
Dagmar Schwerk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Hamburg from ~2011 to 2017 under doctoral supervisor Dorji Wangchuk.
